title: What a named researcher or critic would most likely believe or agree with
subtitle: Central Ideas and Details · 8 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **8 of the official questions in Central Ideas and Details are this one** — 0 Easy, 3 Medium, 5 Hard.
It is top-heavy: most versions are Hard, so it only earns study time once your target actually requires that tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- The stem names a person from the passage and asks what they 'most likely believe' or 'would most likely agree with'.
- The passage reports that person's argument, usually against a common view ('however, X challenges...').

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Isolate that person's claim and ignore the view they are arguing against.
- 2) Apply their claim to what the question asks about: extend the argument to the new situation, don't just repeat it.
- 3) Choose the option that follows from their reasoning.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: The top distractor states the view the person rejects, such as the conventional division or the usual search criteria, because the passage explains that view clearly.
Others push the person's position too far, to 'can't be categorized at all' instead of 'less different than claimed'.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
The top distractor states the view the person rejects, such as the conventional division or the usual search criteria, because the passage explains that view clearly.
Others push the person's position too far, to 'can't be categorized at all' instead of 'less different than claimed'.
